proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly distinguishes sūjī “needle, small awl”, from sūcikā, from the semolina and tailor homonyms. CDIAL 13551,1 includes sūcikā in its needle head as well as the contracted sūī family. The survey j/z forms therefore belong to this needle family, with the voiced medial consonant retained in the analysis. Regional learned or vernacular transfer remains unresolved; the link does not treat j as an arbitrary spelling of zero.
